newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks rebound on late speculative buying.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks rebound on late speculative buying.

text.p: Mexican stocks recovered in late trading to close higher Tuesday after speculative buyers stepped into the market.
"This morning's falls were on thin volume, and then prices were ripe for some speculative buying," a trader at the Bancomer brokerage said.
The leading IPC share index ended up 16.49 points, or 0.45 percent, at 3,652.99 points. Volume was 81.5 million shares.
The Dow Jones industrial average closed up 27.32 points, or 0.40 percent, at 6,833.48 points.

The U.S. Federal Reserve began a meeting Tuesday and is expected to make an announcement Wednesday, when Mexican financial markets will be closed for Constitution Day. Most analysts expect policy-makers at the Fed, the U.S. central bank, to hold interest rates steady.
Equity analysts noted that buying was mainly confined to Mexican blue chips.
"Gains are still very selective. Blue chips are hauling up the IPC, although a few brokers are rearranging portfolios with market stragglers,' one analyst said.
A total of 107 stocks changed hands, of which 56 gained while 29 declined.
Beverage firm Gemex B and CPO shares topped the gainers' list, up 60 (eight cents) and 84 centavos (11 cents), respectively, to 3.20 pesos (41 cents) and 12.94 ($1.65).
Dealers said Gemex gained on news it had acquired a stake in Monterrey-based bottler Agral.

Financial groups Serfin and Crece topped the losers, falling 24 (three cents) and nine centavos (one cents), respectively, to 2.63 (34 cents) and 1.15 pesos (15 cents). Dealers noted that financial companies were not expected to post favourable 1996 earnings on the basis of reports by other groups announced thus far.
